content.text:
I've submitted, and the episode is over. The best composition I measured is **index 66** (Bi 0.039, Cu 0.577, V 0.384), with a photocurrent of **6e-8 A**. I used all 3 merit measurements and none of the XRD budget.

| Index | Bi | Cu | V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.267 | 0.432 | 0.302 | 0 |
| 100 | 0.076 | 0.551 | 0.373 | 3e-8 |
| 66 | 0.039 | 0.577 | 0.384 | 6e-8 |

- **Why I aimed at low Bi:** the light is 2.06 eV (602 nm). BiVO4's band gap is about 2.4 eV, so it barely absorbs at that energy. Copper vanadates near a Cu:V ratio of 3:2 have gaps of about 2 eV, so I targeted that low-Bi region first.
- **Trend:** photocurrent roughly doubled each time the Bi fraction dropped. That points to a copper-vanadate phase doing the work, but three points can't prove it.
- **Why I skipped the model's last pick:** after two measurements, the model's pick (index 24) had an uncertainty larger than its predicted value. I spent the last measurement on the lowest-Bi composition instead.

**Caveats:**
- I didn't take any XRD, so I haven't confirmed which crystal phase is actually present at index 66.
- About 10 other low-Bi compositions near index 66 (such as 68, 72 and 77) were never measured and could beat it. With only 3 measurements, index 66 is the best of what I tested, not a confirmed library maximum.
